{{Recipe summary
| Category = Beverage recipes
| Difficulty = 4
}}

{{recipe}}

'''White house honey porter''' is the much-anticipated recipe to White House beer.<ref>{{cite web |url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220711171805/https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/blog/2012/09/01/ale-chief-white-house-beer-recipe|title= Ale to the Chief: White House Beer Recipe|last= Kass|first= Sam|date= 01-09-2012 |website= The White House|publisher= The White House|access-date= 30-07-2022|quote=}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 2 (3.3) [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] cans light unhopped [[Cookbook:Malt|malt]] extract
* ¾ [[Cookbook:Pound|lb]] Munich [[Cookbook:Malt|Malt]] (cracked)
* 1 lb crystal 20 malt (cracked)
* 6 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]] black malt (cracked)
* 3 oz chocolate malt (cracked)
* 1 lb White House [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* 10 [[Brewing/Ingredients#Bittering|HBU]]<nowiki/>s bittering [[Cookbook:Hops|hops]]
* ½ oz Hallertaur Aroma hops
* 1 pkg Nottingham dry [[Cookbook:Yeast|yeast]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Corn sugar|corn sugar]] for bottling

== Procedure ==
# In a 6 [[Cookbook:Quart|qt]] pot, add grains to 2.25 qts of 168°F water. Mix well to bring the temperature down to 155°F. Steep on [[Cookbook:Cooktop|stovetop]] at 155°F for 45 minutes. Meanwhile, bring 2 gallons of water to 165°F in a 12 qt pot. Place [[Cookbook:Strainer|strainer]] over, then pour and spoon all the grains and liquid in. Rinse with 2 gallons of 165°F water. Let liquid drain through. Discard the grains and bring the liquid to a boil. Set aside.
# Add the 2 cans of malt extract and honey into the pot. Stir well.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] for an hour. Add half of the bittering hops at the 15 minute mark, the other half at 30 minute mark, then the aroma hops at the 60 minute mark.
# Set aside and let stand for 15 minutes.
# Place 2 gallons of chilled water into the primary fermenter and add the hot wort into it. Top with more water to total 5 gallons if necessary. Place into an ice bath to cool down to 70-80°F.
# Activate dry yeast in 1 cup of sterilized water at 75–90°F for 15 minutes. Pitch yeast into the fermenter. Fill airlock halfway with water. [[Cookbook:Fermentation|Ferment]] at room temp (64–68°F) for 3–4 days.
# Siphon over to a secondary glass fermenter for another 4–7 days.
# To bottle, make a priming syrup on the stove with 1 cup sterile water and ¾ cup priming sugar, bring to a boil for five minutes. Pour the mixture into an empty bottling bucket. Siphon the beer from the fermenter over it. Distribute priming sugar evenly. Siphon into bottles and cap. Let sit for 1–2 weeks at 75°F.
